project: BHU LOKA (भूलोक) · Sovereign Earth & Climate Workstation
challenge: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 - Dancing with the SARs

study_area.name: Patna & Ganga Floodplain, Bihar, India
study_area.river_confluence: Ganga, Gandak, Son, and Punpun Rivers

methodology.technique: Dual-Date Logarithmic Backscatter Difference & Otsu Physical Water Thresholding
methodology.why_sar_matters: Active microwave C-band (5.405 GHz) radar penetrates dense monsoon cloud cover and operates day/night. During the September 2019 Patna deluge, optical satellites (MODIS / Landsat / Sentinel-2) were 100% blind due to overcast monsoon skies.

scientific_integrity_audit.data_authenticity: 100% OBSERVED Copernicus Sentinel-1 C-SAR via ASF Vertex
limitations: 10-meter spatial resolution cannot resolve narrow sub-resolution alleys (<10m).
Strong surface winds may roughen open water causing Bragg scattering and increased backscatter.
Radar shadow from tall urban concrete structures may mimic low-backscatter water.
No live in-situ river gauge is embedded in the pixel; values represent calibrated dielectric/geometric surface properties.
